children.topic: Primary Diagnostic Test: Osmotic Fragility Test (hemolysis starts at 0.6% saline)
Key Pathological / Cell Marker: Spectrin & Ankyrin deficiency
Role & Indications for Splenectomy: Splenectomy is the only cure. Best performed at 6–7 years of age.
Primary Diagnostic Test: Indirect Coombs' Test (identifies RBC surface antibodies)
Key Pathological / Cell Marker: IgG anti-RBC autoantibodies
Role & Indications for Splenectomy: Indicated upon failure, contraindications, or severe complications of corticosteroids.
Primary Diagnostic Test: Hb Electrophoresis (absence of Hb-A, high Hb-F)
Key Pathological / Cell Marker: Globin chain synthesis defect; "Hair-on-end" skull X-ray
Role & Indications for Splenectomy: Indicated in select cases strictly to decrease the rate and volume of repeated transfusions.
Primary Diagnostic Test: Platelet count & Bone marrow biopsy (hyperplastic megakaryocytes)
Key Pathological / Cell Marker: Anti-platelet autoantibodies
Role & Indications for Splenectomy: Indicated if ITP has persisted for >6–9 months. Transfuse platelets ONLY after splenic artery safety ligature is tied.
